ishrouded-glade.title: Shrouded Glade

wiki_page.title: Shrouded Glade
wiki_page.text:
Shrouded Glade is a town in northeastern Sacred Grove. It is nestled at the base of Misty Mountain and wrapped in the thick and mysterious mist that gives the glade its name. Shrouded Glade is the home of the Druid Academy, and the druids keep the entire town neat and orderly.
thumb|350px

History
Shrouded Glade has always been a home for the druids, though the Elder Council wasn't officially formed until after the Unbinding. Unwilling to let their ancient knowledge fade away, the remaining druids banded together and formed the Academy to not only expand on their existing knowledge but to instruct those who were worthy enough to become druids themselves. Within the Academy's walls they built a library filled with all the books there could salvage from the ruined Athenaeum.

On June 15th, 2012, Shrouded Glade was invaded by the Gloam. The landscape became corrupted and evil entities siege the city, called Shrouded Gloam. The event included a new questline, along with open world combat. 

Travel
Shrouded Glade is only accessible through a tunnel or by a warpstone. The main road from the tunnel leads directly to the Druid Academy, which sits above the Glade between a pair of mighty waterfalls and the river that flows from them. All roads and rivers radiate outward from the Academy in wide rings, as if they were ripples in a still pool.

Shrouded Glade also have a different bridge near the Druid Academy that lead to Sunstone Valley.

isunstone-valley.title: Sunstone Valley

wiki_page.title: Sunstone Valley
wiki_page.text:
Sunstone Valley is a desert area that can be found on the Atlas on a northern extension created among it's arrival. It has open world combat, where enemies roam the land and attack approaching players. Once a player has been defeated, they are prompted to revive in a safezone or spend 1,000 coins to receive on the spot of defeat. When an enemy is defeated, there is a possibility that the player will receive a loot drop; clothes, crafting ingredients, recipes, or consumables. Different enemies types will drop different loots, but all enemies will have a chance to drop a small amount of coins.

Inhabitants of Sunstone Valley range from large reptilian humanoids known as manguanas, frontier robgoblins, feathered drakes, rocklars and Biker Dwarves.
thumb|300px
Selections
There are selections in the Atlas, with two locations that are viewable.

South is Sacred Grove, near the Rough Rider Raceway, where players can encounter.

North is Glimmerdeep, near the Rocklar Village. Players couldn't travel there because its entrance is blocked by the barrier.

Sub-Regions
In Sunstone Valley, it's split into sections.

The first being is Pony Vale, where the Mystical Barrier is next to another area where Sandspear is found in, and the water path is on there where you have to swim there.

The last being is the Rocklar Village, where it is near the Drakewind Peak, and the rock bridge is there where you have to walk there.

Selections
There are selections in the Atlas, with some locations that are viewable. 

North is Silver Hills, near Snowhill where the Crystal Barrier is there. Players can't travel there because its entrance is blocked by the Crystal Barrier.

North-east is Sunstone Valley, near Shrouded Glade where players could encounter.

South is Lavender Coast, near Greenwood Forest where the Lavender Coast Pass warpstone is near. Players couldn't travel there because its entrance is blocked by barriers.

East is Black Forest, near Stillwater Crossing, where players  could walk to the bridge in the mountain. Players couldn't travel there because its entrance is blocked by barriers.

wiki_page.title: Silversnow
wiki_page.text:
Silversnow is a pixie NPC that can be found in Snowhill. He is an elderly man who has been waiting in front of the Crystal Barrier for hundreds of years. He waited for the Crystal Barrier to open, and to finally be reunited with the Elves on the other side. Silversnow carried a box of fruitcake he had prepared for the Elves' return.

wiki_page.title: Dartmoor Quarry
wiki_page.text:
The Dartmoor Quarry is a mining corporation that is on a mountainous range, its precious ore visibly sticking out of the earthen ground. It is located southeast of Wugachug and west of Highroad Junction. Various races of Sacred Grove flock to this location for the precious tin and topaz that can be mined here.

A favored place of amateur miners that are level 5+. Some explorers, looking for rare tokens in their adventures, may find the Dartmoor Quarry is an excellent place to scour the grounds of.

wiki_page.title: Quagmire Quarry
wiki_page.text:

It was originally a dwarven silver mine, but it was abandoned at the time of the Unbinding. The mine is currently haunted by many of it's former miners, and infested by giant spiders.

Silver is mined here by level 15+ Miners.

isunset-of-free-realms.title: Sunset of Free Realms

wiki_page.title: Sunset of Free Realms
wiki_page.text:
The Sunset of Free Realms is an official term used by Sony Online Entertainment representatives when referring to the closure of Free Realms on March 31, 2014 at 6:00 PM pacific time, 7:00 Mountain time, 8:00 Central time, and 9:00 Eastern time.

On January 24, 2014, an article by Free Realms Producer Steve "Shock" George was released over the official Free Realms website announcing the closure of Free RealmsWith Heavy Hearts, We Announce the Sunset of Free Realms on Free Realms, later reposted on the official forums and official wiki. Along with Free Realms, closure was announced for three other Sony Online Entertainment massively multiplayer online games including: Clone Wars Adventures, Vanguard: Saga of Heroes, and Wizardry Online.

Reasons for closure of the game were given by SOE's President, John Smedley, over Reddit. It was not a big cost issue, but more of an issue with the amount of time it required to maintain the code bases when updating authentication or security updates,chooseareality comments on I'm John Smedley, President of SOE. AMAA on Reddit.com and that the resources were needed elsewhere.Cyliena comments on I'm John Smedley, President of SOE. AMAA on Reddit.com Along with SOE will no longer be developing games exclusively aimed towards children.FirePuff comments on I'm John Smedley, President of SOE. AMAA on Reddit.com

Free Realms Sunset FAQ
On February 18, 2014, Free Realms Community Relations Manager Tiffany "Amnerys" Spence posted answers to Frequently Asked Questions, concerning the sunset, over the Official Free Realms forums.Free Realms Sunset FAQ on Free Realms Forums

Dates

params.Row 5 info: [[wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online game|Massively multiplayer online]] [[wikipedia:Adventure game|adventure game]]

wiki_page.title: Free Realms
wiki_page.text:
This article contains information all or in part from Wikipedia.You can help the Free Realms Wiki by [ De-Wikifying it].

Free Realms was a Massively Multiplayer Online Adventure video game developed by Sony Online Entertainment set in a fantasy-themed world for the PC, Mac and PlayStation 3. The game was released on April 28, 2009 for the PC. The PS3 version was released in 2011. On January 28, 2014, Sony Online Entertainment announced that the game would be closed on March 31, 2014.

John Smedley, president of Sony Online Entertainment(SOE), revealed that one million users had signed up to Free Realms 18 days after its launch; a month after release Free Realms reached two million users, and on June 12, 2009, reached 3 million users.

Gameplay
Players are able to choose from Jobs (classes) such as Adventurer, Ninja, Postman, Medic, Archer, and formerly Pet Trainer which became unavailable after December 14, 2009, and switch on the fly without creating a new character. The game limits barriers to entry and encourages social gameplay where, regardless of level or class, players will be able to interact, join forces and play together. There are many worlds to go to and a large number of quests to complete for coins and stars to help level up the character's job. Leveling up is handled in several ways, ranging from traditional combat to quests and minigames depending on which job the player wishes to advance.

Unlike typical MMOs, combat is completely optional and the focus instead, is spread across a variety of gameplay mechanics – exploration, combat, building, housing, pet-raising, mini-games and social networking – to ensure its appeal to a variety of audiences.

Momma Meepster was introduced in-game as a part of the 8-Bit Month on September 10th, 2013.

istone-heart.title: Stone Heart

wiki_page.title: Stone Heart
wiki_page.text:
Stone Heart is an enemy NPC boss featured as the main antagonist of the Festival of Hearts. He is a heart-shaped monster, his main goal while arrived is to destroy the Love Potions in Merry Vale which will break all the people's love.

Biography
Before the Festival of Hearts, Rylan and Arianna who were two lovers met long ago and came together near a flower that grew every time they were near each other. One day, dark magic fell over the land and Rylan never showed up again. He went out on the day of dark magic, he got turned into Stone Heart. He gathered the changelings around him. Stone Heart has no love and sees the festival as an insult. He will try to crush as much of the special magic as he can so others will be as lonely as he is.

Battle
Open World
During the time that Stone Heart is arrived, bring sadness and the feeling of heart break to all the people in love. He will slowly walk along the pathways of Merry Vale giving players time to confront the boss, the Love Potions appear on the pathways of Merry Vale. The Love Potions temporarily grant players an enchanted bow with the ability to attack Stone Heart and stop the Heart Breakers from stealing Valentine Love.

Once defeated, Stone Heart drops a special treasure chest that rewards the players that assisted in that specific battle a Festival of Hearts themed item. If he wins, he will successfully destroy the Love Potion that will break all the people's love and disappear which him and the Heart Breakers ruin the Festival of Hearts in Merry Vale, which will not drop anything.

Stone Heart's Hideaway
While Stone Heart doesn't appear in Merry Vale, but instead a Heart Breaker. Encounter the battle which at one point will require you to encounter in a battle which requires you to be level 13 combat job or above t

iroyal-vault.title: Royal Vault

wiki_page.title: Royal Vault
wiki_page.text:
The Royal Vault was a underground entrance underneath the entrance bridge of Sanctuary to two doors that could be accessed inside and containing chests with lots of items like clothes, shards, weapons, etc. It had a members and a non-members door into getting items. To be able to access the vault you needed to only enter it as if it was a minigame/battle, once you were inside the Royal Vault you needed only Treasure Tickets which were able to get by doing any quest from people in Sacred Grove to open the chests that contained the items.

Inside the non-members Royal Vault entrance you had 3 chests to decide from contained of any job and any item. The non-members chests were from the prices 30 tickets for a good item or an okay item for 20 tickets or a cheap item for 10 tickets. The Members Royal Vault entrance had 16 chests to decide from and all of the chests were containing all amazing items from all jobs that were available but also a consumable items chest, these chests needed about 30 tickets to be able to open.

Why was the Royal Vault closed?
thumb|246px|Glush and the now closed Royal Vault

Members of Free Realms development team have stated that the vault was closed in an effort to enhance the reward systems available within the game. One of the primary mechanics added to the game after the closure was a prize wheel available when a player successfully completes most of the minigames or dungeons.

Additionally, game designers felt that the tickets required to redeem prizes within the Royal Vault were essentially another type of currency along with Coin and Station Cash. This means that removing tickets as a currency was also on of the objectives accomplished by closing the Royal Vault.

Other reasons for closing the Royal Vault have been speculated widely, alth

wiki_page.text:
Bryce, also known as Ghostshadow, is an NPC ninja, and is the oldest and most experienced of the Realmkeepers. He seems to be the strong and stoic leader of the group, as the team rallies around him. His deck is Order, and his signature weapon is the Blade of the Mist. His ride is a dragon named "Drake".

There also is an outfit that can be gained by opening a Heroes TCG pack, along with the others (Magetech, Wildclaw, and Crackshot). His ride is also obtainable in the pack. From the Hero's TCG questline, in which the player is tasked to defeat Baron von Darkcheat, other items such as in-game posters could be obtained.

wiki_page.title: Necronomicus
wiki_page.text:
Necronomicus is a fairy NPC boss featured as the main antagonist of the Southern Wilds chapter of the Heroes Journal. He is the Gloam Lord of Necromancy, and is currently the only Gloam Lord in the game at this time. He mainly resides in the Fairy Cultist territory.

Quest
Mysterious Stranger
During the quest named Bixie-B-Gone, a mysterious NPC with the name plate, the Mysterious Stranger is found near the missing caravan. It is later found out the Mysterious Stranger had been Necronomicus.

Locations
Necronomicus (Temporary Quest NPC)
A little bit south of Queensfields next to the missing caravan. Disappears once talked to.

Necronomicus (Battle Boss NPC)
May be found in the battle "Necronomicus Unleashed" which can only be unlocked by getting the quest "Necronomicus Unleashed" from the Fighter's Guild Message Board in Sanctuary.

Necronomicus (Overworld Enemy NPC)
May be found via a secret passage that the player may only gain access to after completing a certain quest in the Heroes Journal.

Versions
There are two different Necronomicus enemy versions and an intractable Necronomicus NPC that can only be interacted with once in order to complete a quest for the Southern Wilds questline.

Battle

thumb|300px|Necronomicus' skeletal form
This is Necronomicus Unleashed, the difficulty 5 battle. As its description suggests, this battle is designed as a group assault, and it will require you to encounter Necronomicus in a battle which requires you to be level 13 combat job or above to enter. Through progression of the Heroes Journal Merry Vale quest, a Overworld combat battle will become available during the quest named Unmasking the Villain.

The house has a large yard, with an out-in-the-country feel to it. There are large trees and rocks adorning the lot, as well as many flowers and other plants. Around the edge of the property is a dark brown picket fence, as well as a curved gate at the entrance to match.

thumb|360px|Interior view of the Small Wilds House.Small Wilds House on ZAM|left

The house itself is quite tall, with a staircase leading up to the porch that is as long as the house's width. The outside is a light aqua with light brown accents. There are around 9 windows, 3 of them being portholes. The inside is very open, leaving enough space to work with for the player's imagination. The wallpaper is green, but is red on the other side divider, and the floors are plain wood with an orange tint to them. However, both the wall paper and flooring, including the exterior, can be changed with purchases from the Coin Shop or SC Marketplace.

Dimensions
The dimensionsFree Realms Detailed Housing Guide on GuideScroll of the Small Wilds House are:
 Height 39 Blocks
 Width 47 Blocks
 Length 36 Blocks
 Volume 65,988 Blocks

wiki_page.title: Glimmerdeep
wiki_page.text:
Glimmerdeep was an unreleased location that was never opened to denizens of Sunstone Valley. It would've been located north between the Rocklar Village and the Drakewind Peak, there is the hydropower dam which its entrance is blocked by the barrier.

Very little is know about that, Whirly Willis mention that robgoblins were cut off from Glimmerdeep to creating a junk supply shortage during the quest titled A Deal with a Dust Devil.

Like other unreleased locations, Glimmerdeep was never added to Free Realms before it was shut down on March 31, 2014.

Gallery

Trivia
Glimmerdeep may originally called Bronze Mountains.
Glimmerdeep was the only location to have different barrier on it's entrance in Sunstone Valley.
Glimmerdeep is the second unreleased location there is no concept art for it, first is Black Forest.
Glimmerdeep was the only location that was never mentioned in the Atlas.
It is unknown what Glimmerdeep would've looked like. It is possible that area would've been a cavern or something with crystals.
In the quest titled A Deal with a Dust Devil, Glimmerdeep is referred to as Glimmer Deep by Whirly Willis.

isacred-glade.title: Sacred Glade

wiki_page.title: Sacred Glade
wiki_page.text:
Sacred Glade was the tutorial area where new adventurers were first introduced into the world of Free Realms. After you have run through Sacred Glade at least once, you can then skip the tutorial for each subsequent character created.

Tutorial Beginning
Entering the game
Upon entering the game you will experience a brief 360 degree view around your character.

Michael Tallstrider frantically runs up to you. He was glad you made it through the warpstone before it was destroyed by the robgoblins. He needs your help chasing the creatures off. Click the gray Goodbye button to continue.

Camera and Movement
To move the camera in game, hold down the right mouse button and drag your mouse in the direction you want to look.

Move your character by either:

1. Left click on the ground.

2. Hold down both mouse buttons

3. Use the W,A,S, & D keys

4. Use the arrow keys

NPCs and Quests
Moving down the path, you will see Michael stop and you will learn about NPCs and receiving quests.
 NPCs who have quests for you are designated with a green (!) above their heads.
 If an NPC is part of a quest (as an objective) you will see a green (?) above their head.
 If an NPC has a quest that you are too low to receive, a gray (!) will be above their head.

The quest helper (journal or log) gives you the steps to complete your quests, and updates with each objective completion.
 Non-members can only hold 10 quests before it is full.
 Pressing the gray button of an arrow pointing to a dot will minimize the helper.
 Moving your cursor towards the quest name in the helper will make arrows appear, allowing you to scroll through the quests you have.

Click on Michael and learn that the robgoblins chased a pig from Farmer Chug's pen. Click on the green "Yes, I accept!" button to receive the Tutori

wiki_page.title: Gleam Council
wiki_page.text:
The Gleam Council is the governing body of the precursor civilization during the Age of Harmony. The council was comprised of several members representing the main races found in Sacred Grove.

History
The Gleam Council was formed at the beginning of the Age of Harmony when the major races in Sacred Grove (humans, elves, pixies, dwarves, and chugawugs) came together in a unified civilization. Not much is known of life before their rule and the time period. The tour guide Grayfoot in the Memorial Caverns is on record for describing these members as running the gamut in terms of competence and experience. The council was the central governing body for Sacred Grove and was tasked with ensuring the safety of its subjects. Among the many issues that they presided over was the uncontrolled use of magic, a problem that saw many people hurt and/or killed. The council would have heated debates over how to handle the issue. Their reign would end with the events of the Binding when the Gloam Council usurped them and took control of the region. However, before they were overthrown, they were said to have successfully warned the citizens of what was to come, saving countless lives.  
Category:Groups

wiki_page.title: Underworld
wiki_page.text:
The Underworld was an unused location from the early development of Free Realms where the Pumpkin Prince was mentioned to be in there. Inhabitants of this area are known to be skeletons, and possibly undead monsters.

This area was never planned to be added. 

Gallery

Trivia
In the Pumpkin Prince's battle on the Bone Bog Cemetery, the Underworld is referred to as the ghost world by Lucinda.

Sources
At least while I worked on Free Realms, we hadn’t done a lot of planning for other regions beyond the never-shipped Underworld. Eventually they added Sunstone Valley, of course. on Twitter
For question 2, our Underworld wasn’t scary: it was a 24/7 party!  on Twitter

Category:Dimensions
Category:Unreleased

wiki_page.title: Shapeshifter
wiki_page.text:
The Shapeshifter is a character that appear in the Free Realms Issue 12. She is a shapeshifter that posing as Queen Valerian, and an agent from a cult that wants to destroy Free Realms.

When Dane and the Druid came to a path that near the Shrine of Knowledge, then the Shapeshifter came, and tell Dane to give her the Chaos Amulet. The Shapeshifter used it to summoned the Chaos Beast. At the end of the Free Realms Issue 12, Darkthorne send the Shapeshifter to the Abyss where she will rot for all eternity.

Gallery

Trivia
Despite being a female character, the Shapeshifter hasn't revealed what she would look like in her true form.
The Shapeshifter is the eighth character who don't appear in-game, first was Ayani, second is the Wood Monster, third is Ashlynne, fourth is Elvis, fifth is Ashley Dazzlespark, sixth is Logan Mirehold, seventh was the Guardian, ninth is the Chaos Beast, and tenth is the Stranger.

Free Realms #2 was the second issue in the Free Realms series of comics based on the game of the same name. It was published on October 7, 2009 by Wildstorm.

Publisher's summary
SONY teams with WildStorm and best-selling fantasy author J.S. Lewis (the Grey Griffins series) for an exciting adaptation of Free Realms, their new MMORPG! This 12-issue series mirrors the nonstop action of the game, offering exciting adventures, battles with vicious monsters and, of course, the allure of gorgeous fairies! The story begins when a young girl is abducted and dragged into a darkened forest teeming with twisted monsters. It's up to a relic hunter and a pixie to save him, but their mission is cut short when a horde of troll-like creatures captures them!

Free Realms #3 was the third issue in the Free Realms series of comics based on the game of the same name. It was published on November 25, 2009 by Wildstorm.

Publisher's summary
The 12-issue adventure epic continues from best-selling fantasy author J.S. Lewis (the Grey Griffins series) and artist Jon Buran (WORLD OF WARCRAFT)! Based on Free Realms, the exciting new MMORPG from SONY, this series adapts the nonstop action and thrills of the game, offering exciting adventures, battles and more Dane and Maya return from their dangerous mission into the Briarwood to retrieve the missing girl, but the queen's representatives aren't offering a hero's welcome! Looks like the queen couldn't care less about the young girl and instead wants the box containing the potion that could keep her majesty from dying. But the box is empty! Now Dane and Maya must return to the Briarwood to find the vial before the queen dies... or her fate becomes their own!

igifting-basket.title: Gifting Basket

igd: Place this in your house and click it every day to receive a gift! Turns into a regular holiday basket after 30 days.

wiki_page.title: Gifting Basket
wiki_page.text:
thumb

The Gifting Basket is a housing item that was previously sold through the Station Cash Marketplace during the 2011 Festival of Hearts event. It can no longer be acquired.

When placed in a lot, it cannot be removed for thirty days, similar to the Jackpot Plant. You can move it to a different position in the lot, but that's all you can do until the thirty days are over. At the end of the thirty day period, the Gifting Basket becomes a Holiday Basket, which can be removed.

Rewards

Every 24 hours within the thirty days, the player who purchased the Gifting Basket can click on it for a Festival of Hearts themed reward. Possible rewards include:

 Bleeding Heart T-Shirt, in all 22 colors
 Deathly Love T-Shirt, in all 22 colors

on SOE WordPress BlogA Welcome Back Producer Letter on Free Realms - What is New? As part of the teased Ranching feature, players could hatch the Baby Unicorn from an egg and raise it to be either a pet or a mount.SOE Webcast - Podcast 111 Live at E3 - 6/8/11 on YouTube
